questions.question: Is there any abnormality of the pancreas?
questions.definition: An abnormality of the pancreas is defined as any abnormal finding in the pancreas. This definition includes operative change, a resected part of the pancreas and a normal anatomical variant. This definition excludes a device where nothing else is abnormal.

questions.question: Is there acute pancreatitis?
questions.definition: Acute pancreatitis is defined as acute inflammation of the pancreas, with peripancreatic fat stranding or fluid, diffuse glandular enlargement, or a non-enhancing parenchymal segment. This definition includes an acute episode on a chronic background, necrosis, a peripancreatic collection and a walled-off collection. This definition excludes chronic pancreatitis alone, whose signs are glandular atrophy, parenchymal or ductal calcification, and ductal dilation.

defs.label: Excludes

questions.question: Is there splenomegaly?
questions.definition: Splenomegaly is defined as an enlarged spleen. No single CT measurement defines it. This definition excludes a spleen called normal in size, whatever its measurement.

questions.question: Are there any epithelial splenic cysts?
questions.definition: An epithelial splenic cyst is defined as a true splenic cyst with an epithelial lining, congenital or epidermoid, thin-walled and of fluid attenuation. This definition includes a splenic cyst with no cause given. This definition excludes a post-traumatic, post-infarction or post-infectious cyst.

questions.question: Are there any splenic pseudocysts?
questions.definition: A splenic pseudocyst is defined as a splenic cyst with no epithelial lining, following trauma, infarction or infection. This definition excludes a congenital or epidermoid cyst, and a splenic cyst with no cause given.

questions.question: Is splenic lymphoma present?
questions.definition: Splenic lymphoma is defined as lymphomatous involvement of the spleen, with splenic masses or diffuse infiltration in a patient with lymphoma. This definition excludes splenomegaly alone.

questions.question: Are there any splenic lacerations?
questions.definition: A splenic laceration is defined as torn splenic parenchyma: a laceration, a fracture, or a shattered spleen. This definition excludes a subcapsular or perisplenic hematoma with no parenchymal tear.

defs.label: Definition
defs.text: A splenic laceration is defined as torn splenic parenchyma: a laceration, a fracture, or a shattered spleen.

defs.label: Excludes

questions.question: Are there any splenic infarcts?
questions.definition: A splenic infarct is defined as a non-enhancing area of splenic parenchyma, wedge-shaped or global, from vascular occlusion. This definition excludes a devascularized segment attributed to trauma.

defs.label: Definition

questions.question: Is the spleen absent?
questions.definition: An absent spleen is defined as no spleen in the splenic fossa, from any cause. This definition includes a splenectomy, congenital asplenia, and an autosplenectomy.

defs.label: Definition

questions.question: Are there any accessory spleens?
questions.definition: An accessory spleen is defined as a splenule, a small round nodule of splenic tissue near the splenic hilum, in the splenic ligaments, or in the pancreatic tail. This definition excludes splenosis after a splenectomy.

questions.question: Are there any sites of active extravasation in the spleen?
questions.definition: Active extravasation in the spleen is defined as contrast material leaking from a vessel into the splenic parenchyma or around it, as a contrast blush or a jet of extravasated contrast. This definition includes a pseudoaneurysm that is actively leaking. This definition excludes a hematoma with no contrast leak.

questions.question: Are there any post-splenectomy changes in the splenic bed?
questions.definition: Post-splenectomy change is defined as operative change in the splenic bed after a splenectomy: clips or sutures, a surgical bed or cavity, or splenosis. This definition excludes an absent spleen with no operative change.

questions.definition: An abnormality of the bile ducts is defined as any abnormal finding in the bile ducts. This definition includes operative change and a normal anatomical variant. This definition excludes the gallbladder, and a device where nothing else is abnormal.

questions.question: Is there any intrahepatic biliary ductal dilation?
questions.definition: Intrahepatic biliary ductal dilation is defined as dilated, prominent or obstructed intrahepatic bile ducts. This definition excludes a dilated extrahepatic duct beside normal intrahepatic ducts.

questions.question: Is there any extrahepatic biliary ductal dilation?
questions.definition: Extrahepatic biliary ductal dilation is defined as dilation of the common hepatic duct, the common bile duct, or both. This definition includes a common bile duct wider than about 6 mm, allowing roughly 1 mm per decade over 60 and up to about 10 mm after a cholecystectomy. This definition excludes a dilated intrahepatic duct beside a normal common duct.

questions.question: Is there any abnormality of the liver?
questions.definition: An abnormality of the liver is defined as any abnormal finding in the liver. This definition includes operative change, a resected part of the liver, a transplanted liver and a normal anatomical variant. This definition excludes the bile ducts, the gallbladder, and a device where nothing else is abnormal.

questions.question: Is there cirrhosis?
questions.definition: Cirrhosis is defined as cirrhotic morphology of the liver: a nodular contour, a shrunken right lobe, or hypertrophy of the caudate or the left lobe. This definition excludes hepatic steatosis alone and chronic liver disease short of cirrhosis.

questions.question: Is there portal hypertension?
questions.definition: Portal hypertension is defined as raised portal venous pressure, with a portosystemic collateral: esophageal, gastric, splenorenal or mesenteric varices, or a recanalized paraumbilical vein. This definition excludes splenomegaly alone, ascites alone, and a dilated portal vein alone.

questions.question: Is there a prior liver resection?

This definition includes a segmentectomy, a partial hepatectomy and a lobectomy. This definition excludes a small or atrophic liver with no sign of surgery and a transplanted liver.

This definition includes a chronically occluded vein, cavernous transformation, tumor thrombus, and thrombus at the splenoportal confluence that extends into the portal vein. questions.definition: A surgically absent gallbladder is defined as a gallbladder removed at a cholecystectomy. This definition includes surgical clips in an empty gallbladder fossa, and biliary ductal dilation attributed to a postcholecystectomy state. This definition excludes a contracted or poorly distended gallbladder, and a normal or unremarkable gallbladder, which the patient still has.

questions.question: Is there acute cholecystitis?
questions.definition: Acute cholecystitis is defined as acute inflammation of the gallbladder: wall thickening together with pericholecystic fluid or fat stranding, or mural hyperenhancement, or gallbladder distension with a stone impacted at the neck. This definition includes acalculous cholecystitis, and an acute episode on a chronic background. This definition excludes gallstones alone, and chronic cholecystitis alone, whose signs are a contracted, thick-walled gallbladder with stones.

questions.question: Is there a prior hysterectomy?
questions.definition: A prior hysterectomy is defined as surgical removal of the uterus: a surgically absent uterus, or an absent uterus with a vaginal cuff. This definition includes a supracervical hysterectomy with the cervix retained. This definition excludes a uterus present but abnormal, and an oophorectomy with the uterus in place.

questions.question: Is there any abnormality of the bones or body wall?
questions.definition: An abnormality of a bone or the body wall is defined as any abnormal finding in a bone or the body wall. This definition includes operative change, a resected or amputated bone, degenerative or spondylotic change, and a normal anatomical variant. This definition excludes a device where nothing else is abnormal.

questions.question: Are there any fractures?
questions.definition: A fracture is defined as a break in the cortex of any bone in the imaged volume, of acute or indeterminate age. This definition includes a rib fracture. This definition excludes an old, healed, chronic or remote fracture and a chronic deformity.

questions.question: Are there any rib fractures?
questions.definition: A rib fracture is defined as a break in the cortex of one or more ribs, of acute or indeterminate age. This definition excludes an old, healed, chronic or remote fracture.

categories.name: Pleura and lung bases
categories.description: Findings visible in the lower thorax

questions.question: Is there any abnormality of the pleural spaces or lung bases?
questions.definition: An abnormality of a pleural space or a lung base is defined as any abnormal finding in a pleural space or a lung base inside the imaged volume. This definition includes operative change, a lung or a lobe removed at surgery, and a normal anatomical variant. This definition excludes a device where nothing else is abnormal.

defs.label: Definition
defs.text: An abnormality of a pleural space or a lung base is defined as any abnormal finding in a pleural space or a lung base inside the imaged volume.

defs.label: Includes
defs.text: This definition includes operative change, a lung or a lobe removed at surgery, and a normal anatomical variant.

defs.label: Excludes
defs.text: This definition excludes a device where nothing else is abnormal.

include_terms: a pleural effusion or pleural fluid
pleural thickening or a pleural plaque
atelectasis, basilar collapse or volume loss
a pulmonary nodule or mass at a visible lung base

questions.question: Is there any pleural effusion?
questions.definition: A pleural effusion is defined as fluid in a pleural space at a visible lung base. This definition includes a hemothorax and a hydropneumothorax. This definition excludes pleural thickening with no fluid.

defs.label: Definition
defs.text: A pleural effusion is defined as fluid in a pleural space at a visible lung base.

defs.label: Includes

defs.label: Excludes

questions.question: Is there any abnormality of the ureters or bladder?
questions.definition: An abnormality of a ureter or the bladder is defined as any abnormal finding in a ureter or the bladder. This definition includes operative change, a surgically absent bladder, and a normal anatomical variant. This definition excludes the kidneys, and a device where nothing else is abnormal.

defs.label: Excludes

questions.question: Are there any ureteral stones?
questions.definition: A ureteral stone is defined as a calculus in a ureter, at any level including the ureterovesical junction.

defs.label: Definition
defs.text: A ureteral stone is defined as a calculus in a ureter, at any level including the ureterovesical junction.

questions.question: Are there any bladder stones?
questions.definition: A bladder stone is defined as a calculus in the bladder. This definition includes a stone in a bladder diverticulum. This definition excludes a stone at the ureterovesical junction, which is ureteral.

defs.label: Definition

questions.question: Are there any ureteroceles?
questions.definition: A ureterocele is defined as cystic dilation of the distal ureter, ballooning into the bladder lumen. This definition excludes a ureteral stone at the ureterovesical junction.

defs.label: Definition
defs.text: A ureterocele is defined as cystic dilation of the distal ureter, ballooning into the bladder lumen.

defs.label: Excludes

questions.question: Are there any urothelial carcinomas of the bladder?
questions.definition: Bladder urothelial carcinoma is defined as a malignant tumor of the bladder urothelium, also called a transitional cell carcinoma. This definition excludes bladder wall thickening with no malignant diagnosis.

defs.label: Definition
defs.text: Bladder urothelial carcinoma is defined as a malignant tumor of the bladder urothelium, also called a transitional cell carcinoma.

defs.label: Excludes

questions.question: Is there bladder rupture?
questions.definition: Bladder rupture is defined as a breach of the bladder wall, with contrast or urine leaking intraperitoneally or extraperitoneally. This definition includes a wall defect with adjacent extravesical fluid, where no leak is demonstrated.
